Instructional Designer, Course Development
Lanternwise
Remote (US)
Full-time

About Lanternwise

Lanternwise is an online learning platform that partners with universities and companies to offer courses, professional certificates, and degrees to learners around the world. Our mission is to provide universal access to world-class learning. Learners come to us to start new careers, move up in the ones they have, and learn something new for its own sake.

About the team

The Course Development team works with university and industry partners to turn their expertise into courses that learners actually finish. We sit between subject-matter experts, video production, and the product teams that build the learning platform. We care about learner outcomes: completion, assessment performance, and whether learners can apply what they learned.

About the role

We're looking for an Instructional Designer to partner with instructors and subject-matter experts on new courses and professional certificates. You'll own the learning design for a set of courses from first outline to launch, and then use learner data to improve them after launch. Many of our instructors are experts in their field but new to online teaching. You'll be their guide.

This role is a great fit for someone who has designed learning for real learners, whether in a classroom, a university, or a corporate setting, and who wants to work at scale.

What you'll do

- Lead the learning design for 3–5 courses at a time, working with instructors and subject-matter experts from kickoff through launch.
- Write learning objectives, course outlines, and module structures using backward design.
- Design assessments, including quizzes, peer-reviewed assignments, and hands-on projects, that measure the stated objectives. Write clear rubrics and feedback.
- Coach instructors on scripting and recording effective short videos, and review scripts for clarity and learner engagement.
- Build and QA course content in our authoring tools.
- Apply accessibility and inclusive design standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) across all course materials.
- Review learner data, including drop-off points, item performance, and learner feedback, and recommend and make improvements to live courses.
- Contribute to our shared design templates, playbooks, and training for instructors.

What we're looking for

- 3+ years of experience designing learning experiences, in K-12, higher education, or corporate learning.
- Solid grounding in instructional design principles and models, for example backward design, ADDIE, or similar.
- Experience writing assessments and rubrics aligned to learning objectives.
- Experience building courses in a learning management system (Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, or similar).
- Strong writing and editing skills. You can turn expert jargon into plain, clear language.
- Comfort managing several projects and stakeholders at once, with deadlines.
- Experience working with accessibility standards for digital content.

Nice to have

- A master's degree in instructional design, education, learning sciences, or a related field.
- Experience with item analysis or using learner data to revise content.
- Experience with authoring tools such as Articulate Rise or Storyline.
- Experience training other educators or subject-matter experts.
- A portfolio of course or learning design work. Please include a link with your application.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role in the US is $95,000 to $120,000. The final offer depends on skills, experience, and location. This role is also eligible for equity and our benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, a learning stipend, paid parental leave, and flexible time off.

Location and setup

This role is remote within the United States. You'll work mostly on US time zones with the Course Development team and partners. Expect occasional travel for a team offsite or a partner visit, typically 1–2 trips a year (under 10%).

Work authorization

We will consider candidates who require visa sponsorship, including H-1B transfers, for this position.

How to apply

Submit your resume and a link to your portfolio or work samples. If you don't have a public portfolio, a short description of one learning experience you designed, including who it was for, what you built, and what you learned from testing it, is welcome instead.

Lanternwise is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.
